content.text:
Measured, so here's the actual rule.

## The rule

`--depth N` fetches **exactly N commits**. `HEAD~K` needs **N ≥ K+1**.

| Your range | Minimum depth |
|---|---|
| `--base HEAD~1` | 2 |
| `--base HEAD~3` | **4** |
| `--base HEAD~10` | 11 |

Verified on a real clone: depth 4 runs fine; depth 3 fails **loudly**, not silently —

```
resolve diff base "HEAD~3": fatal: Needed a single revision
```

## Why I said 25, not 4

Headroom, for three things you'll actually hit:

1. **Changing range on the spot.** A judge asks "what about a bigger diff?" — at depth 25 you just run `--base HEAD~10`. At depth 4 you re-clone mid-demo.
2. **Pinning to a SHA that isn't HEAD.** `git checkout b3f4d83` only works if that commit is inside the fetched window. If upstream has moved 6 commits past your pin, depth 4 no longer contains it.
3. **A dud range.** If `HEAD~3..HEAD` turns out to be all docs or CI, you need somewhere else to go.

Depth 25 costs a few seconds and about 75MB on Django. Not worth optimising.

## Verify before you rely on it

```sh
git rev-parse HEAD~3 >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "range OK" || echo "TOO SHALLOW"
git rev-list --count HEAD          # how many commits you actually have
```

## If you're already too shallow — no re-clone needed

```sh
git fetch --deepen=50      # add 50 more commits
git fetch --unshallow      # or get the whole history
```

## The one case where depth won't help

**Tag-to-tag diffs.** `--base 5.1 --head 5.2` needs both tags in history, and a shallow clone fetches no tags by design. Use either:

```sh
git clone --shallow-since=2025-01-01 https://github.com/django/django.git
# or just take the full clone — Django is ~500MB
git clone https://github.com/django/django.git
```

That's the route to take if you want a **big** change set to show off review ordering — `HEAD~3` on a quiet week gives you 81 entities, whereas a release-to-release diff gives you hundreds, which is much closer to the "47-file agent PR" the pitch is about.

+// claim reduces a reason to the part that differs between findings, dropping
+// the rationale clause that follows ", so ".
+// The rationale is identical everywhere it appears — "…, so its symbols can be
+// invoked by name at runtime and an absent call edge is not evidence of an
+// absent caller" is 104 characters and, on Django, printed more than twenty
+// times: once per risk finding, again inside each finding's verify comment, and
+// again beside each of 96 listed files. What actually varies is the four words
+// naming the module.
+// So the clause is printed once, in the legend, and every site carries only its
+// distinguishing half. Nothing is withheld; the same sentence is simply not
+// repeated until a reader stops seeing it. Reasons with no ", so " are
+// unchanged, which covers every parse-failure message.
+func claim(reason string) string {
+  if head, _, found := strings.Cut(reason, ", so "); found {
+    return strings.TrimSpace(head)
+  return strings.TrimSpace(reason)
+// runtimeRationale is the clause claim() removes, stated once.
+const runtimeRationale = "a symbol reached by name at runtime leaves no call edge, " +
+  "so an absent edge here is not an absent caller"
+// command strips the trailing shell comment from a verify hint when that
+// comment merely restates the finding printed directly above it.
+// The hint is built by attaching the reason as a "# …" comment, which is useful
+// in isolation and pure duplication in place: the same sentence appears two
+// lines earlier as the summary. What a reader needs from this line is the
+// command they can paste.

content.text:
Fixed and validated on your actual Django run.

## What was wrong

The 140-character rationale — *"…so its symbols can be invoked by name at runtime and an absent call edge is not evidence of an absent caller"* — was printed **more than 20 times**: once per risk finding, again inside every `verify:` comment, and again beside each of 96 listed files. Only four words ever varied.

## What changed

**1. The rationale is stated once, in a legend.** Each finding keeps only its distinguishing half:

```
before: ...(this file imports importlib (dynamic import by name), so its symbols can be
        invoked by name at runtime and an absent call edge is not evidence of an absent
        caller) — the 44 shown is a floor, not a count
after:  ...(this file imports importlib (dynamic import by name)) — the 44 shown is a floor, not a count
```

**2. `verify:` lines are now bare commands.** The trailing `# <same sentence as two lines above>` is gone — unless the comment says something new, which is kept.

```
before: verify: rg -n '\bqualname\b' -- '*'   # this file imports importlib (dynamic import…
after:  verify: rg -n '\bqualname\b' -- '*'
```

**3. Blind spots cluster by reason instead of one line per file.** 96 near-identical lines became three headings with exact counts:

```
this file imports importlib (dynamic import by name) — 32 file(s):
this file imports inspect (runtime introspection)    — 60 file(s):
this file imports pkgutil (runtime package walking)  —  4 file(s):
```

## Two mistakes I made and caught

**I initially deleted the wrong half.** Cutting the string at `", so "` also removed `— the 44 shown is a floor, not a count` — the single most important phrase — and left an unbalanced paren. The rationale is a clause in the *middle* of a sentence, so it has to be excised from the middle. Regression test added.

**My first pass suppressed the "never analysed" file paths entirely.** My own test failed and it was right to: HTML and Vue **can** hide a caller — that's precisely why they aren't in the inert list. Suppressing their paths would have reduced disclosure to save space. Now bounded to 3 per reason with exact counts, not hidden.

Also added `EditorConfig` and `Pip Requirements` to the inert list — they were being listed as blind spots (390 now, was 393).

## Verification

```
gofmt              clean
go build ./...     clean
gate package       65 tests, 88.1%
go test ./...      all packages pass
django run         exit 1, 177 lines
```

Line count barely moved (173 → 177) but the density did: the repeated sentence is gone, and the file listing is grouped. If you want it shorter still, the lever is `reviewOrderLimit` / the per-reason caps — say the word.

content.text:
There are **two different "depths"** in play, which is probably the confusion. They're unrelated.

## First — what the command means, word by word

```sh
entire-graph gate --repo . --base HEAD~3 --head HEAD
```

| Part | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `entire-graph` | the binary you built |
| `gate` | the subcommand — "should this change survive?" |
| `--repo .` | analyse the repo in the current directory |
| `--base HEAD~3` | **start** of the range: 3 commits back |
| `--head HEAD` | **end** of the range: the latest commit |

So it reads: *"Look at everything that changed across the last 3 commits, and tell me whether it's safe."*

Defaults are `--base HEAD~1 --head HEAD`, so a bare `entire-graph gate --repo .` judges just the last commit. `HEAD~3` is only because a 3-commit window gives a meatier demo.

You can put any git ref on either side:
```sh
--base main --head HEAD          # my branch vs main  ← the realistic PR case
--base HEAD~10 --head HEAD       # last 10 commits
--base 5.1 --head 5.2            # release to release
--checkpoint abc123              # an Entire checkpoint instead of a range
```

## Second — the two depths

### Depth 1: `git clone --depth N` — how much history you download

Nothing to do with Gate. It's a git download setting.

**Rule: `--depth N` gives exactly N commits, so `HEAD~K` needs `N ≥ K+1`.**

| Range you want | Minimum clone depth |
|---|---|
| `HEAD~1` | 2 |
| `HEAD~3` | **4** |
| `HEAD~10` | 11 |

Measured — at depth 3, `HEAD~3` fails loudly:
```
resolve diff base "HEAD~3": fatal: Needed a single revision
```

I said 25 purely for headroom: it lets you switch to a bigger range on the spot, and lets `git checkout <pinned-sha>` work if upstream has moved past your pin. Costs seconds. Don't optimise it.

Check before relying on it:
```sh
git rev-parse HEAD~3 >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo OK || echo "TOO SHALLOW"
git fetch --deepen=50     # fix without re-cloning
```

### Depth 2: `--hops 1|2` — how far Gate walks the dependency graph

**This** is Gate's own setting, default `2`.

- `--hops 1` → *who calls this directly?*
- `--hops 2` → *…and who calls them?* (default)

Capped at 2 deliberately. At 3 hops, any utility function pulls in most of the repository and the blast radius stops meaning anything.

## So what does the command actually tell you?

Three things, in order of usefulness:

1. **A ranked reading order** — of Django's 81 changed entities, which 5 to read first
2. **What nobody checked** — `57 unchecked`, each with the dependents that make it matter
3. **A verdict + exit code** — `continue` / exit 1, so it can gate a `git push` or a CI step

Plus the honesty layer: `?` means the graph couldn't see, and the number is a floor rather than a count.

The binary lives in the repo; it's not installed system-wide. Three ways to fix, pick one:

## Quickest — use the full path

```sh
~/buildathon/entire-graph/entire-graph gate --repo . --base HEAD~3 --head HEAD
```

## Better for a demo — put it on PATH for this shell

```sh
export PATH="$HOME/buildathon/entire-graph:$PATH"
```

Then `entire-graph gate --repo . --base HEAD~3 --head HEAD` works from anywhere, exactly as you typed it. Add that line to `~/.zshrc` to make it permanent.

## Cleanest — symlink it once

```sh
ln -sf ~/buildathon/entire-graph/entire-graph /usr/local/bin/entire-graph
```

Survives new terminals, and the symlink auto-follows every rebuild.

---

**For the demo I'd use the `export PATH` line**, run it once in the terminal you'll present from, and verify before you're on stage:

```sh
which entire-graph          # should print the path
entire-graph version        # prints: dev
```

One caution: if you `export PATH` in one tab and demo in another, it won't carry over — `export` is per-shell. The symlink doesn't have that failure mode.
